newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland's markka expected to strengthen - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Finland's markka expected to strengthen - analysts.

text.p: The Finnish markka is on a sharp rising trend against the German mark and should continue to appreciate as overseas demand is heavy and the economic outlook for this year is good, analysts said on Friday.
The recent surge in the U.S. dollar has generated interest in peripheral currencies, particularly the Nordic ones, whose economies have stronger than average European growth prospects, they said.
"Due to the strong dollar (foreign investors) have expanded their usual dollar/mark positions to peripheral currencies," said Tarja Heinonen, chief economist at commercial bank Postipankki.
"And in the Nordics, economic growth is above the European average," she added.
SE-Banken's Helsinki chief economist Esko Torsti said the huge 3.8 billion markka current account surplus for November released on Tuesday also supported the firming of the markka.
"(Current account) growth seems set to continue as fast as last year -- which was a record year," he said.
Analysts said it was difficult to be sure about the near-term outlook for the markka as overseas investors are often quick to reverse their positions -- but fundamentals supported further gains.
"On balance, there are strengthening pressures on the markka," Torsti said.
By mid-morning on Friday, the markka was at 2.9815 per mark, just off its earlier 13-month highs at 2.9760.
